item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: 'On This Ground' St. Benedict's Prep Discussion Panel with Anthony DePalma — Tue Nov 3, 6:15 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
This is an Adult School class. Click HERE to register.
"On This Ground" tells the remarkable story of a school that refused to die in a city that almost did. The school is St. Benedict's Prep, the city is Newark, and the extraordinary people who accomplished this are the Benedictine monks of Newark Abbey and the students they've taught for over 150 years. Joining author and longtime Montclair resident Anthony DePalma will be Anthony Badger, a member of the first class in the reimagined St. Benedict's in 1973, and Jared Boone, St. Benedict's class of 2013, who is now program partner for the Schumann Fund for New Jersey. Both men gave back to St. Benedict's by teaching there before moving on to community-based careers. Both lived in Newark during their time as students at St. Benedict's and witnessed the many ways in which the resilience of the monks and their school helped stabilize the city during its darkest days, including the 1967 civil disturbances and the recent pandemic shutdown

item.title: Let's Watch (Guild Room) — Fri Nov 6, 6:00 PM — Guild Room
item.description: A Most Beautiful Thing (2020, 1h35) follows the story of the first African American public high school rowing team in the United States. Formed in the 1990s at Manley High School and based in Chicago’s West Side, the team was made up of young men, many of whom were members of rival gangs. Reuniting after 20 years, the team gets back on the water to prepare to race in the 2019 Chicago Sprints, the largest rowing regatta in the Midwest. In the process, Arshay Cooper, the team’s captain, takes inspiration from the past and reaches out to the Chicago Police Department to show that rowing can bring even people with the most disparate of backgrounds together. A MOST BEAUTIFUL THING explores not only the safety these young men found on the water (where, as the captain reflected, “we were in a place where we could not hear the sound of sirens”), but the trauma of violence and cyclical poverty, examining how these young men were able to support each other in reimagining a different future fo

item.title: Youth Mental Health First Aid Training for ADULTS - November 2026 — Tue Nov 17, 12:00 PM — Virtual
item.description:
Youth Mental Health First Aid is designed for adults who regularly interact with young people ages 12–18. It teaches parents, caregivers, family members, teachers, school staff, and other caring adults how to recognize and respond to mental health or substance use challenges and support a young person who may be experiencing a crisis. The Course will:
Introduce common mental health challenges for youth Review typical adolescent development Teach a 5-step action plan for how to help young people in both crisis and non-crisis situations
Participants will receive certification after completion of all pre and post work, as well as 4 live virtual training sessions. Registration closes 11/10.
Source: MHA of Essex and Morris

item.title: Ontelaunee to Reading Potpourri Hike — Sun Nov 1, 8:30 AM
item.description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this very interesting point to point hike between Ontelauee Lake and Reading. I've selected another Pennsylvania hike instead of shifting areas this time because there may be structures demolished soon that we need to see before it happens. After meeting in Reading at the Dollar General, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to our start point. There are several trails, and some abandoned roads along the lake. Some of it is an abandoned former road that had been used prior to the creation of the lake. We'll weave around on the trail system in an indirect route, and then make our way onto some back roads, through school ball fields, and then south onto a closed road and past an historic bridge. We will continued from here along a few more back roads to the Muhlenberg Rail Trail. We'll take that south just about to our end point. Distance will be about sixteen miles. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374
S

item.description:

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
